ADDED CYCLE 79 (T2), FROM SOURCES COLLECTED BY CYCLE 78. REPEAT-RUN INCONSISTENCY IS A PROPERTY OF THE INSTRUMENT AND NOT A CONFIGURATION ERROR, AND SETTING TEMPERATURE TO ZERO DOES NOT REMOVE IT FOR API-SERVED MODELS. STATUS IS 'proposed' AND THE REASON IS IN THE LAST PARAGRAPH. (1) THE CLAIM AND ITS EVIDENCE. src-0030 (Coqueret et al., arXiv 2607.24372) names FOUR mechanisms, Section 3 headings verbatim: '3.1 Deliberate sampling', '3.2 Silent model updates', '3.3 Floating point rounding', '3.4 Expert routing'. Verbatim: 'Setting T=0 removes deliberate sampling but...does not eliminate all sources of randomness in frontier models served through online APIs.' Abstract verbatim: 'Exact reproduction is therefore generally not possible when using proprietary application programming interfaces.' It demonstrates the point on its own runs, Section 4.2 and Figure 3 verbatim: locally, 'the distribution of statistics based on Gemma-4 deployed locally...is entirely concentrated at a single value under T=0'; via API at T=0, 'the distribution becomes much more concentrated but does not collapse to a single value. Instead, the estimates take only four distinct values (with one occurring only rarely).' Its normative conclusion, abstract verbatim: 'LLM outputs should be treated as draws from a distribution rather than as fixed measurements.' (2) WHY THIS IS STRUCTURALLY IMPORTANT TO THIS ISSUE AND NOT MERELY BACKGROUND. EVERY consistency measurement in this base -- src-0001's CI widths, src-0016's five-run recurrence counts, src-0018's cross-run decision consistency, src-0031's 400 runs -- rests on the unstated assumption that repeat-run variation is a real property of the system under test rather than an artefact of a configuration the experimenter could have fixed. UNTIL CYCLE 78 THIS BASE HAD NO CITATION FOR THAT ASSUMPTION. src-0030 supplies one, and it also supplies the boundary: the assumption is safe for API-served models and NOT safe as a general claim about LLMs, because locally deployed models at T=0 DO collapse to a single value. So the consistency half of this issue is a claim about DEPLOYED CTI SYSTEMS SERVED THROUGH APIS, which is what the CTI sources actually measure, and it should be stated that way rather than as a claim about language models as such. (3) THE MAGNITUDE DATUM, AND THE CONFOUND THAT STOPS IT BEING MORE. src-0031 supplies by a wide margin the largest repeat-run design in this base -- 100 independent runs per model, four models, 400 runs, one unchanged honeypot target, prompt and orchestrator and target held constant (src-0016 uses five repetitions; src-0018 uses a stopping rule with no fixed N; src-0001 reports CI widths without a stated N). Abstract verbatim: 'Claude achieved full exploitation in 61 of 100 runs; Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite in 85; GPT-4o-mini in 56 while deploying 98 unique attack strategies; qwen2.5-coder:14b in 25.' THE CONFOUND, WHICH IS DECISIVE AND MUST TRAVEL WITH EVERY USE OF THOSE NUMBERS: src-0031's temperature is 0.3 for the Ollama, Gemini and OpenAI calls and 1.0 for Anthropic, an asymmetry it does not control for. So its variation includes DELIBERATE SAMPLING as a first-order contributor -- exactly the mechanism src-0030 says T=0 removes -- and src-0031 is therefore NOT a measurement of irreducible instability and its cross-model comparisons are CONFOUNDED BY SAMPLING TEMPERATURE. Its Claude figure is separately contaminated by a documented HTTP 529 capacity event that truncated 39 of 100 runs and is a floor, not a measurement. THE TWO SOURCES THEREFORE FIT TOGETHER BADLY IN ONE DIRECTION AND WELL IN ANOTHER: src-0030 explains why instability cannot be configured away, and src-0031 shows large instability but under a configuration that does not test src-0030's claim. (4) WHY 'proposed' AND NOT 'supported'. src-0030 is an UNREVIEWED PREPRINT (Comments ABSENT and Journal reference ABSENT on arXiv's own metadata), it is econ.GN, and its experiment is corporate-filing sentiment classification -- FURTHER from CTI than src-0013/0014/0015/0016, which the cycle-16 scope ruling already bars from CTI multi-source support. src-0031 is an UNREVIEWED SINGLE-AUTHOR PREPRINT and is security-adjacent penetration testing, which is not IoC extraction, TTP mapping, attribution or report drafting. NEITHER SOURCE MAY BE COUNTED TOWARD CTI MULTI-SOURCE SUPPORT FOR THIS ISSUE and this candidate must not be promoted to 'supported' on the strength of these two alone. WHAT WOULD PROMOTE IT: a peer-reviewed source for the mechanism claim, or a CTI-proper repeat-run study that holds temperature at zero and still finds variation. (5) ONE FURTHER DATUM FROM src-0031 THAT BELONGS TO A DIFFERENT ISSUE AND IS RECORDED HERE ONLY SO IT IS NOT LOST. Section 4.4 verbatim: 'Across 400 runs and four providers, no model produced a content refusal under the -authorized penetration testing- framing used in this study.' It is scoped to ONE framing on ONE target with a one-shot authorization re-prompt and is NOT a general under-refusal rate. It bears on automated-triage-under-refusal, which is NOT this issue, and a T2 does not move it there unasked; note also that src-0031's abstract records the author CORRECTING an earlier draft that had catalogued 91 HTTP 529 errors as safety refusals, which is a caution about how easily an infrastructure failure is misread as a model behaviour.

SUPPORTED, ENTERED CYCLE 80 (T3) AS THE POSITIVE STATEMENT OF WHAT THE CONSISTENCY HALF OF THIS ISSUE ACTUALLY HAS. IT REPLACES NOTHING AND WITHDRAWS NOTHING: candidate_resolutions[4] IS LEFT STANDING PER THE APPEND-ONLY RULE and must be read alongside this entry and ctr-0035, which is RESOLVED at cycle 80. THE CLAIM, IN TWO PARTS THAT MUST NEVER BE COLLAPSED INTO ONE. (1) THE EXISTENCE OF RUN-TO-RUN OUTPUT INSTABILITY ON CTI MATERIAL AT TEMPERATURE 0 IS TWO-SOURCE. src-0001 (academic, ARES 2025, 350 real reports, gpt4o / gemini-1.5-pro-latest / mistral-large-2, fixed 10 re-prompts with a fixed seed) and src-0018 (SentinelLabs, industry lab, five models a generation later, a different CTI corpus, no shared author and no citation in either direction) both report non-zero repeat-run variation in output on CTI extraction material with the temperature parameter set to 0. The independence argument entered at cycle 39 is untouched and was NOT re-examined at cycle 80. (2) VARIATION IN CORRECTNESS ACROSS RUNS IS SINGLE-SOURCE, AND THAT SOURCE IS src-0001. src-0018's two consistency metrics are, BY THEIR OWN PRINTED DEFINITIONS, confined to alternation among values the expert annotators accepted as VALID: 'IOCs with P_o < 1: The proportion of extracted IOCs for which, across repeated runs under identical conditions, the LLM assigned two or more different values for the same attribute, alternating among the values that the expert annotators defined as valid (yielding observed agreement P_o < 1 across runs)' and 'Average mode-based observed disagreement D-bar_o: For the subset of IOCs with P_o < 1, the average proportion of the LLM-assigned attribute values across the repeated runs that differ from the dominant (mode) value'. The source's own gloss of the first, recovered at cycle 80 and new to this base, is 'higher percentages of IOCs with P_o < 1 indicate greater fluctuation in how the LLM interprets ambiguous evidence'. An extraction pipeline can post a strictly positive share of IOCs with P_o < 1 while being CORRECT ON EVERY RUN, because alternating between two valid values is never an error. THE NEGATIVE IS TWO-RENDER CONFIRMED AT CYCLE 80: src-0018's body text was swept on the direct sentinelone.com URL and on the r.jina.ai proxy render for any variance, standard deviation, error bar, interval or count-of-wrong-runs quantity attached to precision, recall, F1 or accuracy. Both forms returned the same two metrics and nothing else; 'variance', 'standard deviation', 'error bar' and 'stability' are ABSENT on both. WHY src-0018 CANNOT BE PATCHED INTO THE GAP, WHICH IS A DEDUCTIVE POINT AND NOT A COMPLAINT ABOUT REPORTING: its stopping rule is 'all reported metric values were obtained through repeated executions of each evaluation experiment until the point estimates reached a 95% confidence level with a relative precision of less than 5%'. A variable-n rule that halts when the interval is narrow enough PINS THE REPORTED INTERVAL WIDTH AT THE THRESHOLD BY CONSTRUCTION, so that width is uninformative about the underlying spread; and because an interval half-width scales as spread over the square root of n, recovering the spread requires n, which src-0018 discloses on NEITHER render. src-0001's fixed-n bootstrapped CI widths (max 0.02 for extraction, 0.06 for generation, over exactly 10 re-prompts) do not have this defect, which is why the two studies are not symmetric here. CONSEQUENCE FOR SCORING, STATED SO THAT A T4 NEED NOT INFER IT: the consistency half of this issue meets a TWO-SOURCE bar for EXISTENCE and a ONE-SOURCE bar for MAGNITUDE-IN-CORRECTNESS. WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT: any second CTI source reporting a FIXED-n spread of a correctness metric across repeated identical queries. NONE IS IN THIS BASE. SCOPE NOTE, BECAUSE THE NEAREST ANALOGUES ARE TEMPTING AND INADMISSIBLE: src-0014, src-0015 and src-0016 measure repeatability on NON-CTI material (code and JavaScript repositories) and are not CTI sources for this purpose under the cycle-16 scope ruling. src-0016's five-repetition finding-signature counts are the closest analogue anywhere in the base and they are on JavaScript vulnerability findings, not on CTI. === CYCLE 90 G2 RE-VERIFICATION OF THIS CANDIDATE. ANSWERED AT CYCLE 28 (T3), after ten cycles in which it was merely articulated. THE QUESTION WAS: did ENISA's APT29/'Midnight Blizzard' naming-convention hallucination (src-0004) contribute to, or correlate with, the kind of plausible-but-wrong attribution measured quantitatively in src-0002, or is it a distinct hallucination sub-type (citation/naming fabrication vs. attribution judgment)? THE ANSWER IS: DISTINCT SUB-TYPE. THE DECIDING ARGUMENT COMES FROM src-0002'S OWN SCORING RULE, already stored verbatim in this base: 'To further ensure accuracy, we manually verify each LLM response to account for the multiple aliases that threat actors often use.' CTI-TAA SCORES AN ALIAS AS CORRECT -- its 'correct answer' bucket is defined as 'when the LLM accurately identifies the threat actor or one of its aliases'. APT29 and Midnight Blizzard are two names for one group, and the ENISA passage names the right group; its error is the claim about WHICH VENDOR USES WHICH NAME, i.e. a false statement about naming provenance, not a false statement about who conducted the activity. Under CTI-TAA's own rule the ENISA sentence would be scored CORRECT. The ENISA defect is therefore INVISIBLE TO THE MEASUREMENT INSTRUMENT this issue's quantified leg rests on, and the two cannot be instances of one measured phenomenon. Two corroborating considerations, neither load-bearing: the same ENISA report's other documented defect is 26 of 492 incorrect footnotes, a citation-validity failure of exactly the kind src-0011 (GhostCite) and src-0012 (EY Canada) measure; and src-0004 attaches no accuracy or confidence measurement of any kind to the passage. CONSEQUENCE, RECORDED AGAINST THIS ISSUE'S OWN INTEREST: src-0004's evidential home is institutional-incident-real-world-impact, and it must not be counted as an independent second source for THIS issue's central claim -- which is why the primary candidate below now cites src-0002 alone, where it previously cited src-0002 and src-0004. RESIDUAL, GENUINELY OPEN AND NOT TO BE ASSERTED EITHER WAY: whether the two sub-types share an upstream generative cause (both being ungrounded production of a specific-looking fact) is a mechanism question that no source in this base tests.

candidate_resolutions.summary: REWRITTEN AT CYCLE 28 (T3), executing step (i) of ctr-0002's resolution path. THE 86-VS-52 FRAMING IS RETIRED, NOT REPAIRED. The old text of this candidate said 'every one of the 5 tested models' plausible-sounding attribution rate substantially exceeds its correct attribution rate (e.g. GPT-4-turbo: 86% plausible vs 52% correct; Gemini-1.5: 74% vs 38%)'; CTIBench defines Plausible Accuracy as 'the fraction of correct and plausible answers combined', so it CONTAINS Correct Accuracy and that inequality is true by construction for every model on every dataset. It evidenced nothing and is withdrawn. WHAT REPLACES IT. CTI-TAA partitions each response into three buckets, verbatim: 'correct answer (when the LLM accurately identifies the threat actor or one of its aliases), plausible answer (when the threat report lacks sufficient details to pinpoint the answer, but the LLM provides a plausible or related threat actor within a similar group), and incorrect answer (when the LLM misattributes the threat actor due to misjudgment, hallucination, or spurious correlation)'. The THIRD bucket is the paper's own hallucination-inclusive misattribution rate and equals 100 minus Plausible Accuracy: GPT-4-turbo 14%, GPT-3.5-turbo 38%, Gemini-1.5 26%, LLAMA3-70B 20%, LLAMA3-8B 64%, over 50 real threat reports, with the authors stating that they 'manually verify each LLM response to account for the multiple aliases that threat actors often use'. THOSE FIVE VALUES ARE DERIVED BY SUBTRACTION FROM TABLE 1 BY THIS AGENT AND ARE NOT PRINTED ANYWHERE IN THE PAPER; every cell they are derived from was re-verified EXACT against Table 1 by two independent fetches at cycle 23, and the ChatGPT-4 row was re-confirmed a third time at cycle 28. THE FINDING: outright misattribution of the threat actor is common in 2024-era models, from roughly one report in seven for the best model to nearly two in three for the weakest, on real reports scored with alias tolerance. WHAT THIS CANDIDATE DOES NOT CLAIM, and the distinction is the whole point of this issue: src-0002 measures WRONGNESS, NOT CONFIDENCE. Its 'plausible' bucket is scoped to UNDERDETERMINED INPUT answered with a related actor from a similar group -- arguably reasonable behaviour under ambiguity -- and is explicitly NOT its hallucination bucket. issues.title: How confidently do LLMs assert threat-actor attributions they get wrong -- and is that quantity measured by anything at all?
open_questions: CREATED AT CYCLE 45 (T2) BY SPLITTING attribution-confident-wrong-gap, per carry-forward [45], which had requested the split since cycle 25. READ THAT ISSUE'S open_questions[3] FIRST -- it records the split in full, including why the OTHER issue kept the now-misleading legacy id 'attribution-confident-wrong-gap' (it is cited from three APPEND-ONLY knowledge files and cannot legally be renamed). THIS ISSUE IS THE LEG WITH NO EVIDENCE, AND THAT IS ITS ENTIRE POINT: it exists so that the well-evidenced attribution-ERROR-RATE leg can be scored on its own merits instead of being held down by a question nothing in this base answers, and so that the unanswered question stays VISIBLE instead of being quietly absorbed as a caveat on somebody else's number. A SUCCESSOR MUST NOT TREAT A LOW SCORE HERE AS A FINDING ABOUT THE WORLD. It is a finding about the evidence base.

THE PRIMARY OPEN QUESTION, AND IT IS A COLLECTION QUESTION BEFORE IT IS AN ANALYTIC ONE: does ANY published evaluation measure expressed confidence on threat-actor attribution -- verbalised confidence ('I am 80% sure'), token-level probability, hedging rate, refusal/abstention rate, or a calibration statistic such as ECE or Brier computed ON AN ATTRIBUTION TASK? NO SOURCE IN THIS BASE DOES, as of cycle 45 and as surveyed at cycle 28. [SENTENCE REPAIRED AT CYCLE 49 -- THE TEXT THAT STOOD HERE FROM CYCLE 45 TO CYCLE 48 WAS FALSE.] What stood here was 'THIS IS A T1 TARGET AND NO SCHEDULED TASK CURRENTLY REACHES IT', and it is withdrawn. Cycle 48 first doubted it and cycle 49 re-read prompts/t3_investigate.md at source and confirmed: step 2 reads VERBATIM 'Work through the open questions using the existing knowledge base FIRST. Only web-search for what the knowledge base cannot answer (and if you fetch something substantial, add it properly as a source per T1 rules -- it counts toward the same max_new_sources budget).' A T3 IS EXPLICITLY AUTHORISED TO WEB-SEARCH AND TO ADD SOURCES when the base cannot answer, which is precisely this issue's condition. THIS ISSUE WAS NEVER STARVED; it was simply never scheduled until cycle 49, which did collect against it (src-0023, src-0024) under exactly that clause. The starvation premise behind carry-forward [96] and [55] is withdrawn. No contradiction entry was opened for this because G3's trigger is two SUPPORTED CLAIMS in conflict and an open_questions annotation is not a candidate_resolution -- the precedent is cycle 26 and ctr-0010. Note precisely what would and would not count: a calibration number on a DIFFERENT task set does NOT count (see the next question), and an accuracy or error rate does NOT count at any exchange rate, because a model can be uniformly wrong while being uniformly hedged or uniformly strident and the error rate cannot distinguish those cases.

WHY THE NEAREST-LOOKING EVIDENCE DOES NOT TRANSFER, RECORDED SO NOBODY RE-DISCOVERS IT AND SO NOBODY IMPORTS IT ANYWAY. The base DOES contain confidence and calibration measurements -- src-0001's and src-0013's ECE and Brier scores -- but they are computed on ENTIRELY DIFFERENT TASK SETS and belong to consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode, which is listed in this issue's depends_on for exactly that reason. The genuinely open question is whether calibration behaviour measured on those tasks TRANSFERS to attribution, and NOTHING IN THIS BASE TESTS TRANSFER. Until something does, importing an ECE from another task to stand in for attribution confidence would be an operationalisation mismatch of the shape this project has already booked twice. THE THREE SOURCES CLOSEST TO THIS ISSUE ALL FAIL IT FOR STATED REASONS: src-0002 partitions CTI-TAA outputs by CORRECTNESS ONLY (correct / plausible / incorrect) and records no confidence construct of any kind, and its 'plausible' bucket is scoped to UNDERDETERMINED INPUT answered with a related actor from a similar group -- arguably reasonable behaviour under ambiguity, and NOT a confidence measurement; src-0007's 'Content: Threat Actor' block is an LLM-judged 1-5 QUALITY rubric whose absolute level is uninterpretable and which, per ctr-0008, measures SOURCE LINKING rather than actor identification in its 'Attribution' row; src-0004 is a single published passage with no measurement attached at all. Also note, from src-0002's own text, that the exact string 'plausible-sounding' DOES NOT OCCUR IN THE PAPER, though this project presented it in scare quotes as a quotation for 27 cycles -- the phrase in this issue's ancestry is OURS, not a source's.

A DESIGN QUESTION THIS ISSUE SHOULD NOT DUCK, because it determines whether the issue is answerable in principle: WHAT WOULD THE RIGHT MEASUREMENT EVEN LOOK LIKE? Attribution is unlike the tasks calibration is normally measured on, because the ground truth is itself contested, aliased and sometimes genuinely underdetermined by the report -- which is precisely why CTIBench needed a 'plausible' bucket and why it scores an ALIAS as correct. A confidence measurement that ignored that would be measuring the wrong thing. So a well-posed target is narrower than 'is the model calibrated': it is whether a model's expressed confidence DISCRIMINATES between reports whose attribution is determined by the evidence and reports whose attribution is not. If no published work measures that, saying so with this reasoning attached is a legitimate resolution of this issue and should be recorded as such rather than treated as a failure to find an answer.

ADDED AT CYCLE 49 (T3, THE FIRST TASK EVER AIMED AT THIS ISSUE). SCOPE OF THE EXTERNAL SEARCH, RECORDED BECAUSE A NEGATIVE FINDING IS WORTH NOTHING UNLESS ITS SCOPE IS STATED. Five web searches were run, in these directions: (1) verbalised-confidence and calibration on threat-actor attribution specifically; (2) abstention/refusal rate plus ECE/Brier on a CTI attribution task; (3) CTIArena and other current CTI benchmarks against confidence/calibration/abstention; (4) 'threat attribution' with overconfidence/hedging/uncertainty; (5) uncertainty quantification and confidence elicitation applied to APT-group identification. WHAT CAME BACK: a large and active general-domain literature on verbalised confidence, calibration and abstention (ConfidenceBench, I-CALM, Abstain-R1, 'Wired for Overconfidence', LLM-as-Judge overconfidence, black-box UQ surveys) and a separate CTI-benchmark literature that measures CORRECTNESS ONLY. THE TWO DO NOT MEET ON AN ATTRIBUTION TASK IN ANYTHING CYCLE 49 FOUND. The single most probative new artefact, src-0023 (arXiv 2510.11974, ACCEPTED TO KDD 2026, with a Threat Actor Profiling task in v1 and an Entity Attribution task category in v2), returned ABSENT on two URL forms serving two different versions for every one of: calibration, Expected Calibration Error, ECE, Brier, confidence, likelihood, abstain, abstention, 'I don't know', 'insufficient evidence', uncertain, logprob, 'how certain'. SEPARATELY AND INDEPENDENTLY, the released CTIBench artefact was checked at source (src-0019, evaluation/evaluation.ipynb): its CTI-TAA scorer compute_taa_accuracy computes correct-and-plausible accuracy from a string-connection helper and NOTHING ELSE, and the strings confidence, calibration, probability, abstain, abstention, unknown, refus, hedge, ECE, Brier and logprob are ALL ABSENT from the entire notebook. So for the benchmark this issue's ancestry was built on, the absence of a confidence construct is now confirmed IN THE EXECUTABLE CODE and not merely in the prose. THIS IS THE SECOND, DIFFERENTLY-SHAPED CONFIRMATION THAT METHODOLOGICAL RULE (v) REQUIRES FOR AN ABSENT VERDICT.

ADDED AT CYCLE 49. WHAT GENUINELY REMAINS OPEN, REPLACING THE BLANKET 'NOBODY HAS LOOKED' THAT PRECEDED IT. (a) THE STRONGEST UNCHECKED LEAD IS INSIDE THIS BASE AND NOBODY HAS PULLED IT: src-0015 (OpenSec) defines its reward with the verbatim clause 'Attribution rewards correct identification (+1 per correct field) and penalizes unknowns (-0.5 each)' -- an explicit PENALTY ON ABSTENTION attached to a component the paper itself calls Attribution. That is the closest construct in this base to an abstention measure on an attribution task. IT IS NOT YET A COUNTEREXAMPLE TO THIS ISSUE'S SURVEY FINDING, for two stated reasons: it is a TRAINING-SIGNAL component rather than a reported measurement, and OpenSec's 'Attribution' is incident-field identification inside synthetic RL episodes, not threat-actor identification from a threat report. BUT NOBODY HAS CHECKED WHETHER OpenSec REPORTS AN UNKNOWN-RATE OR ABSTENTION-RATE ANYWHERE, and if it does, this issue's primary question changes shape. This is a cheap, well-specified next action against a source already in the base. (b) src-0023's Appendix D PROMPT TEMPLATES were unreadable in both fetches, and prompt templates are exactly where an instruction to state a confidence level would live -- under rule (xvi) that absence is NOT established; the ar5iv render or the KDD 2026 proceedings would close it. (c) The MISP taxonomy LEVEL SETS behind src-0024 were not fetched, so this base cannot yet say how many levels admiralty-scale or estimative-language define or what they are. (d) UNCHANGED AND STILL THE DEEPEST GAP: whether calibration behaviour measured on other task sets TRANSFERS to attribution is tested by NOTHING, in this base or in anything cycle 49 found. (e) Note for the record that cycle 49's searches were English-language, and that a benchmark could measure this in an appendix a search engine does not index -- the finding is 'not found by these searches', which is weaker than 'does not exist', and must always be stated that way.

candidate_resolutions.summary: SURVEY FINDING, RESTATED FRESH AT CYCLE 45 (T2) FROM THE (b) HALF OF attribution-confident-wrong-gap's candidate_resolutions[1], WHERE IT WAS ESTABLISHED AT CYCLE 28 AND WHERE IT REMAINS AS THE AUDIT RECORD. It is restated rather than moved so that no text was cut out of the other issue. THE FINDING: NO SOURCE IN THIS KNOWLEDGE BASE MEASURES EXPRESSED CONFIDENCE ON THREAT-ACTOR ATTRIBUTION. src-0002 partitions outputs by correctness only -- its metric section defines accuracy for CTI-MCQ and CTI-RCM, MAD for CTI-VSP, F1 for CTI-ATE, and the three-bucket correct/plausible/incorrect partition for CTI-TAA, and nothing else -- so it records no verbalised confidence, no hedging rate, no calibration metric and no reader-facing plausibility judgement, and no sentence in the paper interprets the correct-versus-plausible gap. src-0007's 'Content: Threat Actor' block is an LLM-judged 1-5 quality rubric that grades attribution QUALITY rather than how confidently the model asserts it, and per ctr-0008 its 'Attribution' row measures SOURCE LINKING rather than actor identification. src-0004 is a single published passage with no measurement attached at all. THE STATUS IS 'supported' AND WHAT IT SUPPORTS IS A CLAIM ABOUT THE EVIDENCE, NOT ABOUT THE WORLD: it does NOT show the confident-but-wrong gap is small, large, or absent. It shows that nobody in this base has measured it, and that NO CYCLE MAY TREAT AN ATTRIBUTION ERROR RATE AS A PROXY FOR IT. The three source ids are cited as the evidence for the SURVEY -- i.e. these are the sources that were read and found not to measure the quantity -- which is the only sense in which a negative finding can carry evidence at all, and it is stated explicitly here so that a T4 does not mistake this for three sources SUPPORTING a positive claim.

CYCLE 49 (T3), THE FIRST TASK EVER AIMED AT THIS ISSUE, EXTENDED THE SURVEY BEYOND THE KNOWLEDGE BASE AND THE ANSWER DID NOT CHANGE: NO PUBLISHED EVALUATION FOUND BY A FIVE-DIRECTION EXTERNAL SEARCH MEASURES EXPRESSED CONFIDENCE ON THREAT-ACTOR ATTRIBUTION. The previous candidate was a claim about THIS BASE; this one is a claim about what a targeted search of the published literature returns, and it is deliberately kept separate rather than merged, because the two have different scopes and different failure modes. THE POSITIVE CONTENT OF THE NEGATIVE: there are TWO healthy literatures here and they do not intersect on attribution. One measures verbalised confidence, calibration, selective prediction and abstention in general domains and is large and current. The other -- CTIBench (src-0002), CyberThreat-Eval (src-0007), CyberSOCEval (src-0005), and now src-0023, a KDD-2026-accepted benchmark with an explicit Threat Actor Profiling task -- evaluates CTI attribution BY CORRECTNESS ONLY. src-0023 returned ABSENT for calibration, ECE, Brier, confidence, likelihood, abstain, abstention, uncertain, logprob and 'how certain' across two URL forms serving two different versions of the paper. INDEPENDENTLY, the CTIBench artefact's own executable scorer (src-0019) was read at source and computes correct-and-plausible accuracy and nothing else, with every confidence-related string ABSENT from the notebook -- so for the benchmark this issue descends from, the absence is now confirmed in CODE as well as in prose. That is the second, differently-shaped confirmation methodological rule (v) demands. STATUS IS 'supported' AND WHAT IT SUPPORTS IS A CLAIM ABOUT THE LITERATURE, NOT ABOUT MODELS: it does not show that LLMs are, or are not, confidently wrong when attributing. It shows that the quantity is still not being measured, by anyone cycle 49 could find. SCOPE LIMIT STATED HONESTLY: this is 'not found by five English-language searches plus targeted checks of the nearest benchmarks', which is weaker than 'does not exist', and no cycle may upgrade it to the stronger form.

THE DESIGN QUESTION IN open_questions[3] NOW HAS AN ANSWER, AND IT COMES FROM OPERATIONAL HUMAN PRACTICE RATHER THAN FROM ML: THE MEASUREMENT THIS ISSUE ASKS FOR IS ALREADY A STANDARDISED, MACHINE-READABLE CONSTRUCT -- IT HAS SIMPLY NEVER BEEN APPLIED TO AN LLM ATTRIBUTION EVALUATION. open_questions[3] worried that attribution may be unlike the tasks calibration is normally measured on, because attribution ground truth is contested, aliased and sometimes genuinely underdetermined by the report -- which is why CTIBench needed a 'plausible' bucket -- and concluded that the well-posed target is narrower than 'is the model calibrated': it is whether expressed confidence DISCRIMINATES between reports whose attribution is determined by the evidence and reports whose attribution is not. src-0024, the MISP threat-intelligence best-practice on expressing confidence, shows that human CTI practice resolved exactly this by SPLITTING THE JUDGEMENT IN TWO. It names two taxonomies and gives verbatim tag examples 'estimative-language:likelihood-probability="almost-no-chance"' and 'estimative-language:confidence-in-analytic-judgment="moderate"', alongside 'admiralty-scale:source-reliability="a/b/c..."'. LIKELIHOOD-PROBABILITY grades how likely the claim is to be true; CONFIDENCE-IN-ANALYTIC-JUDGMENT grades confidence in the judgement itself, i.e. in the sufficiency of the evidence and reasoning -- and the two are tagged separately and can move independently. THE SECOND AXIS IS PRECISELY THE QUANTITY open_questions[3] DERIVED, UNDER AN OPERATIONAL NAME. CONSEQUENCE, AND IT IS THE USEFUL PART: the objection that attribution confidence is too ill-posed to measure because the ground truth is contested DOES NOT HOLD. A well-posed evaluation is constructible today -- elicit both axes on an attribution task and test whether confidence-in-analytic-judgment tracks evidential determinacy while likelihood tracks correctness -- and CTIBench's own correct/plausible/incorrect partition, whose 'plausible' bucket is scoped by src-0002's verbatim definition to reports that LACK SUFFICIENT DETAIL to pinpoint the answer, already supplies a determinacy label to test against. THIS IS A DESIGN CLAIM, NOT A MEASUREMENT. src-0024 contains no LLM, no model and no number, and may never be cited as evidence about model behaviour. Per this issue's own standing permission, recording that no published work measures this WITH the reasoning attached is a legitimate resolution rather than a failure to find an answer -- and this candidate is that resolution's constructive half.

issues.title: Is 'AI-generated CTI reliability' a single property, or does it vary sharply by task type (mechanical extraction vs. open-ended reasoning)?
open_questions: SPLIT NOTE (cycle 16, T2, discharging carry-forward [1] after it was carried unactioned for nine consecutive cycles). This issue now covers ONLY the narrow claim: that AI-generated CTI reliability varies sharply by sub-task rather than being a single uniform property. The SPECIFIC ORDINAL AXIS ('mechanical extraction < classification < attribution < generation'), together with the cycle-2 proposed cross-source synthesis that carried it and the open question about whether a better explanatory variable exists, was MOVED VERBATIM to the new issue 'extraction-vs-reasoning-ordinal-axis'. The reason for the split is that the two claims have very different evidential status and were sharing one issue and one candidate_resolution from cycle 2 to cycle 15, which is exactly why no T4 could score either honestly: the narrow claim has five independent supporting sources (src-0001, src-0002, src-0006, src-0007, and now src-0013 on the calibration axis) while the ordinal axis is actively disputed between src-0006 and src-0007. Do NOT re-merge them.

src-0006's causal-intervention mitigations raised an attribution-adjacent task (Threat Actor Linking) by only +0.055 accuracy, a much smaller gain than LANCE's ~72-86%->97.6% F1 jump on IoC extraction (src-0003) -- but the two are not a controlled comparison (different tasks, metrics, mitigation types: automated retrieval/inference intervention vs. human-in-the-loop regex+LLM pipeline). No source yet tests a LANCE-style human-validated pipeline specifically on ATT&CK mapping or attribution; a search this cycle for such a study (and for RAM/src-2502.02337, an automated non-human-in-the-loop ATT&CK mapper) found none. Does human-in-the-loop validation specifically (not just any targeted mitigation) transfer to reasoning-heavy tasks, and if so how much of the IoC-extraction gain would it recover?

Since src-0003's strong result is single-study/in-house, would the task-dependence conclusion survive an independent replication showing a smaller IoC-extraction advantage? A cycle-6 search for independent LANCE/PRISM replication or critique found none published yet.

candidate_resolutions.summary: The core, narrower claim -- that AI-generated CTI reliability is genuinely task-dependent rather than a single uniform property -- is now supported, not just proposed: src-0006 (cycle 6) directly measures reliability across multiple distinct CTI sub-tasks within one consistent study design (rather than only via cross-benchmark synthesis across different teams/models) and finds F1/AUC ranging roughly 0.20-0.90 by specific sub-task, corroborating the cross-study pattern already visible in src-0001/0002/0003/0005. However, the SPECIFIC ordinal axis proposed above (mechanical extraction < classification < attribution < generation) is not confirmed by this evidence and is likely too coarse: src-0006 found its failure patterns cut across all 4 CTI pipeline stages it defines, including extraction/contextualization-type tasks, rather than concentrating in 'reasoning' stages. So: task-dependence itself = supported; the specific extraction-vs-reasoning explanatory axis = open, and now positively questioned rather than merely unverified.

ADDED cycle 16 by T2 at the split. Two further within-study measurements strengthen the NARROW claim -- that CTI reliability varies sharply by sub-task rather than being one uniform property -- and both are of the strongest available kind, holding team, corpus, models and harness constant and varying only the sub-task. (1) src-0007: on one expert-annotated corpus drawn from a real company's CTI workflow, the same four models reach IoC-extraction precision 0.8240-0.8846 while scoring 0.2787/0.2270 (GPT-4o) and 0.3480/0.1759 (o3-mini) precision/recall on MITRE ATT&CK TTP identification, and GPT-4o scores 1.140 out of 5 on the threat-actor Attribution rubric against 3.612 out of 5 for root-cause content in the same table -- roughly a 3x spread across sub-tasks with everything else held constant. (2) src-0013 extends task-dependence to a NEW AXIS that no prior source in this base had tested: reliability varies by sub-task not only in accuracy but in CALIBRATION. Within one study, functional calibration is consistently worse than security calibration for every model tested (delta ECE -0.15/-0.16 GPT-4o-mini, -0.26/-0.27 Gemini-2.0-Flash, -0.52/-0.53 Qwen3-Coder-Next). SCOPE LIMIT ON (2), do not strip it: src-0013 measures secure code generation, not CTI, so it corroborates the SHAPE of task-dependence on a security-adjacent task rather than replicating it on CTI material -- see the cycle-16 scope ruling recorded in 'consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode', which declines to treat security-adjacent corroboration as CTI multi-source support. PROVENANCE ASYMMETRY: src-0007's figures were re-verified verbatim by cycle 15's G2 and are exact to four decimal places; src-0013's are single-pass fetches whose results tables have never been pulled whole (carry-forward [20]). This candidate supports TASK-DEPENDENCE ONLY and deliberately takes no position on the ordinal ranking of sub-tasks, which was moved out of this issue to 'extraction-vs-reasoning-ordinal-axis' at the cycle-16 split.

issues.title: Is there a valid ordinal difficulty ranking across CTI sub-tasks (mechanical extraction < classification < attribution < generation), or is the extraction-vs-reasoning binary too coarse to explain where reliability breaks down?
open_questions: CYCLE-18 HEADLINE, and it changes what this issue is asking. The commensurable measurement that the 'WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY SETTLE THIS' question below demanded ALREADY EXISTS IN THIS KNOWLEDGE BASE and has since cycle 6: src-0006's Table 2 contains nine rows all reported in F1, over ONE corpus and ONE 15-model set (printed column order G5, Go4, CLD, GEM, LL70, MIX, QWN, GRK, FSC, CB0, ZYS, LLY, CBS, SPT, DHT; 8 general-purpose then 7 cybersecurity-specialised), spanning both ends of the proposed ordering. Restricted to those nine rows the yardstick does not change between sub-tasks, which is exactly the property src-0007 lacks. The table was pulled whole and recomputed at cycle 17, then pulled again from a second URL form and recomputed independently at cycle 18 -- cycle 17's state edits were reverted by the validator, so cycle 18 is the first time this finding has landed. THE ORDERING IS NOT REPRODUCED. Mean F1 across all 15 models, Contextualization ('extraction') stage: IOC Normalization 0.656, Affected Systems 0.650, Attack Infrastructure 0.631, Malware Family Mapping 0.607, stage mean 0.636. Attribution ('reasoning') stage: TTP Extraction 0.673, Infrastructure Reuse 0.612, Relation Graph Building 0.610, False Flag Detection 0.511, stage mean 0.602. Stage gap 0.034 F1 -- about one fifth of the within-Attribution spread (0.511-0.673) and about one eighth of the mean between-model spread on a single task (0.272). The single BEST task in the whole commensurable subset is TTP Extraction at 0.673, an Attribution-stage task, outscoring every Contextualization task including IOC Normalization: the predicted ordering is not merely weak, it is locally inverted at its strongest predicted point. WHAT IS NOW OPEN: (a) does a 0.034 stage gap survive a SECOND commensurable multi-sub-task study; (b) is 0.034 distinguishable from zero at all, given that src-0006 reports no confidence intervals, no seeds and no repeat runs, so this issue cannot presently attach an uncertainty to its own headline number; (c) src-0006's stage labels are the paper's own four-stage pipeline taxonomy and 'Contextualization' is a looser construct than 'mechanical extraction', so a future cycle should test whether re-labelling the nine tasks by output-label-space size rather than by pipeline stage produces a cleaner split.

NEW cycle 18, and it is the strongest replacement hypothesis on the table. On the same nine-row commensurable F1 subset of src-0006's Table 2, the mean BETWEEN-MODEL range within a task is 0.272 (Affected Systems 0.464, False Flag Detection 0.393, Attack Infrastructure 0.371, Patch Recommendation 0.276, TTP Extraction 0.273, Infrastructure Reuse 0.226, Malware Family Mapping 0.155, Relation Graph Building 0.155, IOC Normalization 0.132) and the mean BETWEEN-TASK range within a model is 0.263 (from 0.171 for ZYS up to 0.404 for LL70 and 0.403 for LLY). EQUAL TO WITHIN 0.009. That answers the last inherited open_question below in the affirmative and mis-specifies the axis: task identity is not the dominant explanatory variable, model identity is at least its equal. A further and weaker signal points at CORPUS identity: the same nominal sub-task, ATT&CK TTP mapping, scores F1 0.478-0.751 in src-0006 but a derived F1 of 0.157-0.250 in src-0007 -- a shift of roughly 0.4 on ONE task, larger than any between-task gap either paper reports. That comparison is uncontrolled (task definition, model set, publication year and metric decomposition all differ at once) and is recorded as a lead, not a result. STILL OPEN: is there any study that varies task while holding model fixed and varies model while holding task fixed, reporting variance components rather than leaving them to a reader's arithmetic? No source in this base does.

NEW cycle 18, and it is a caveat on this issue's own headline evidence rather than a question about CTI. Four of the nine commensurable F1 rows in src-0006's Table 2 -- IOC Normalization, Malware Family Mapping, Relation Graph Building, Infrastructure Reuse -- are STRICTLY MONOTONE DECREASING across all eight general-purpose model columns in exactly the printed column order, with unusually smooth decrements. For independent measurements the chance of one row matching a fixed eight-column order is 1/8! = about 1 in 40,320. Cycle 17 counted eleven such rows across all twenty-eight rows of the table and re-pulled ten of them from a second URL form with an explicit instruction to answer 'CANNOT READ' rather than reconstruct; they returned identical cell for cell. Cycle 18 pulled the nine F1 rows again and independently reproduced every cell and every derived mean. So the pattern is as-printed in the paper and is NOT a fetch artefact; its cause is unknown and no cycle should guess at one. It matters because src-0006 is cited by three issues. The cycle-18 headline is deliberately robust to it: dropping all four monotone rows leaves Contextualization 0.641 against Attribution 0.592, gap 0.049, same direction, TTP Extraction still the highest single task. SEPARATELY, AND NOW CONFIRMED BY TWO CYCLES: src-0006's stored key_claim describes 'Infrastructure Reuse peaks at F1 0.754 for a specialized agent vs. 0.688 for a general model', but the 0.688 column is ZYS, which sits inside the paper's cyber-specialised block; the general-purpose peak on that row is G5 at 0.677. The comparison's direction survives, the label does not. A corrective key_claim was APPENDED to src-0006's entry in state/knowledge/index.json at cycle 18 -- nothing was deleted or rewritten -- and state/knowledge/src-0006.md was left untouched.

ANSWERED IN PART BY CYCLE 18, kept verbatim because its closing question is still live. Its premise 'reliability ranging F1/AUC ~0.20-0.90' is loose and is corrected above: the true F1 span of the nine commensurable rows is 0.286 (False Flag Detection, LLY) to 0.882 (Affected Systems, LL70). Its closing question -- is there a better explanatory variable than a coarse extraction-vs-reasoning binary -- now has a candidate answer, model identity, entered as a proposed candidate_resolution below. ORIGINAL TEXT FOLLOWS. MOVED HERE VERBATIM from 'task-dependent-reliability-framing' at the cycle-16 split; originally written by cycle 6. The cross-cutting 'mechanical extraction < classification < attribution < generation' ordinal axis is not confirmed and is now positively in doubt: src-0006 (cycle 6), the first source to measure multiple distinct CTI sub-tasks within one consistent study, found its 3 failure patterns (spurious correlations, contradictory knowledge, constrained generalization) occur across all 4 pipeline stages it defines, including 'contextualization'-type tasks that would loosely be called extraction, with reliability ranging F1/AUC ~0.20-0.90 by specific sub-task rather than cleanly by extraction-vs-reasoning category. Is there a better explanatory variable (e.g. heterogeneity/volatility/ambiguity of the specific task's input data, or the size/discreteness of its output label space) than a coarse extraction-vs-reasoning binary?

CYCLE-18 NOTE, prepended not substituted. I re-examined this pair with src-0006's Table 2 in hand and STILL DECLINE to open a G3 contradiction, for the cycle-10 reason endorsed by cycle 16 and repeated verbatim below. What cycle 18 adds is that src-0007's ordinal reading, stated below as fact, does not survive src-0007's own table: the third rung depends entirely on an unstated normalisation of a 1-5 rubric -- GPT-4o's 1.140/5 becomes 0.228 under x/5 or 0.035 under (x-1)/4, against a derived TTP F1 of 0.2502, so attribution either ties classification or is seven times worse -- and the middle-to-third rung ORDERING REVERSES BETWEEN TWO MODELS IN THE SAME TABLE, since o3-mini's 2.968/5 is 0.594 or 0.492, both ABOVE its derived TTP F1 of 0.2337. The SUPPORTS half of the tension below is therefore weaker than it reads. That is a reason to doubt src-0007's ordinal reading, not a reason to declare the two sources in conflict. (Provenance note for a future cycle: the rubric values 1.140 and 2.968 come from cycle 15's verbatim whole-table pull of src-0007's Table 4 and were re-checked at cycle 16, but they are NOT recorded in state/knowledge/src-0007.md, which notes those rows only as existing. They are traceable to src-0007 through the cycle-15 log.) ORIGINAL TEXT FOLLOWS. THE CENTRAL TENSION, and why NO contradiction entry was opened -- restated in full at the cycle-16 split so that no future cycle re-litigates it from scratch. src-0007's Table 4 SUPPORTS an ordinal reading: on one corpus with one model set, IoC extraction precision is 0.8240-0.8846, ATT&CK TTP identification precision is 0.2787-0.3480, and the threat-actor Attribution rubric score for GPT-4o is 1.140 out of 5 -- mechanical extraction above technique mapping above attribution, which is the ordering the axis predicts. src-0006's Table 5 OPPOSES it: its failure subtypes span all four pipeline stages it defines, e.g. 'Co-mention bias (Type 1.1) -- stages 1234', so the failure MECHANISMS do not respect the ordering. Cycle 10 examined this pair and DECLINED to open a G3 contradiction, reasoning that src-0006 measures where failure mechanisms OCCUR while src-0007 measures where performance LEVELS differ, and that these are compatible rather than conflicting. Cycle 16 re-read both and did NOT overturn that reasoning: a failure mechanism can be present at every pipeline stage while its impact on measured performance is unequal across those stages, and both facts can hold simultaneously. That is precisely why this is an OPEN ISSUE and not a contradiction -- the two sources are not in conflict; the AXIS is simply not established by either of them.

SUPERSEDED BY CYCLE 18, kept verbatim because its commensurability standard is the right standard and cycle 18 met it, not because the question is still open. The bar it sets was cleared by src-0006's Table 2, which cycle 16 did not know contained nine same-metric rows. Its closing instruction -- 'until a commensurable cross-sub-task measurement exists, this issue should not rise above proposed' -- is therefore DISCHARGED and no longer binds a T4. One half of it survives as a finding rather than a question: the commensurability objection FAILS for the extraction-vs-classification rung of src-0007 and HOLDS for the third rung. Solving 2PR/(P+R) for the unreported IoC recall at which each model's IoC F1 would fall to its own derived TTP F1 gives crossovers of 0.1475 (GPT-4o), 0.1354 (o3-mini), 0.1180 (GPT-4o FT) and 0.0887 (GPT-4o-mini FT), every one BELOW that same model's actual TTP recall of 0.2270, 0.1759, 0.1846 and 0.1414 respectively. So if IoC recall were merely as bad as TTP recall, the gap survives for all four models; it breaks only if IoC recall is worse than TTP recall by a further factor of 1.3-1.6, i.e. an absolute recall of 0.09-0.15, which no source in this base reports for report-level extraction. The precision-only omission is a real reporting defect and is NOT an explanation of src-0007's extraction-vs-TTP gap. ORIGINAL TEXT FOLLOWS. WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY SETTLE THIS (cycle 16): a single study measuring ONE commensurable metric across sub-tasks spanning the full proposed ordering, on ONE corpus with ONE model set. src-0007 comes closest and still falls short, because its yardstick changes between rows -- IoC extraction reports precision only (no recall, no F1, and the paper gives no reason for the omission, a fact cycle 15's whole-table pull confirmed is real rather than a fetch artefact), TTP identification reports precision and recall, and drafting reports a 1-5 rubric. Its apparent ordering is therefore partly an artefact of changing the measurement instrument between sub-tasks. Until a commensurable cross-sub-task measurement exists, this issue should not rise above 'proposed'.

ANSWERED BY CYCLE 18, in the affirmative -- see the between-model-versus-between-task entry above (0.272 against 0.263, equal to within 0.009). The AUC 0.912-versus-0.547 pair this question cites was re-verified exact at cycle 17 and is an instance of the pattern rather than an outlier. Kept verbatim because it is the question that turned out to matter most. ORIGINAL TEXT FOLLOWS. Does the ordering, if it holds at all, hold WITHIN a stage as well as between stages? src-0006 reports F1/AUC ~0.20-0.90 across tasks and models including a spread as wide as AUC 0.912 vs 0.547 for two different models on the SAME task (Source Reliability Scoring). If between-model variance on one task is comparable to between-task variance, then task identity is not the dominant explanatory variable and the axis is mis-specified regardless of which way the between-task comparison comes out.

candidate_resolutions.summary: MOVED VERBATIM from 'task-dependent-reliability-framing' at the cycle-16 T2 split; this text was originally written by cycle 2 and its status of 'proposed' is carried over unchanged. It is reproduced here rather than rewritten, and it is the ordinal-axis half of what was previously one conflated issue. ORIGINAL TEXT FOLLOWS. Across the 5 collected sources, reliability of AI-generated CTI is strongly task-dependent rather than a uniform property: narrow, mechanical extraction (IoC extraction, src-0003) reaches near-97% F1 when LLM output is constrained and human-validated, while open-ended reasoning tasks (ATT&CK technique mapping, threat-actor attribution, general threat-intel reasoning: src-0001, src-0002, src-0005) remain unreliable (accuracy ceilings around 52-72%, confidence miscalibration, and plausible-but-wrong outputs) even as model scale increases. This framing is a synthesis of currently-available evidence, not itself directly measured by any single source, and should be treated as a working hypothesis pending the open questions above. CYCLE-16 ANNOTATION, appended not substituted: the part of this text that survives the split into the parent issue is task-dependence itself, which is now supported there by five sources. What remains HERE and remains merely proposed is the ORDERING -- the claim that the extraction-vs-reasoning distinction is what explains the spread. Note also that the strongest number in this text, src-0003's 97.6% F1, is itself one side of the open contradiction ctr-0001, in which src-0007 measures an unscaffolded LLM at 0.82-0.88 precision on the same broad task; if ctr-0001 resolves in favour of the scaffolding explanation, then the top of this proposed ordering is measuring pipeline design rather than task difficulty, and the axis loses its clearest supporting datapoint. CYCLE-18 REJECTION, appended not substituted; the cycle-16 annotation and the original cycle-2 text above are preserved word for word and the provenance header stands. STATUS CHANGED FROM 'proposed' TO 'rejected'. What is rejected is the ORDINAL AXIS ONLY -- the claim that a mechanical-extraction-versus-open-ended-reasoning distinction is what explains the spread in CTI reliability. Task-dependence itself is NOT rejected; it lives, supported by five sources, in the parent issue 'task-dependent-reliability-framing'. REASON: the one commensurable within-study measurement in this knowledge base, src-0006's Table 2 restricted to its nine F1 rows over one corpus and 15 models, puts the Attribution stage only 0.034 F1 below the Contextualization stage while making an Attribution-stage task -- TTP Extraction at 0.673 -- the best-performing task in the entire subset; and src-0007, the source whose numbers this text leans on for the reasoning end, orders its own middle and third rungs OPPOSITELY for GPT-4o and o3-mini, on a rubric normalisation the paper never states. An ordering that is locally inverted at its strongest predicted point in one study, and that reverses between two models of the same family in another, is not a property of the tasks. See this issue's open_questions for the full derivation and its three caveats.

SUPPORTED, entered cycle 18. The identical finding was produced by cycle 17, whose state edits the validator reverted; cycle 18 re-pulled src-0006's Table 2 from a second URL form and re-derived every mean, range and crossover independently before landing it. THE CLAIM: the proposed ordinal axis 'mechanical extraction < classification < attribution < generation' is NOT supported by the only commensurable cross-sub-task measurement available in this base, and the extraction-versus-reasoning binary is too coarse to explain where CTI reliability breaks down. TWO INDEPENDENT ROUTES, from two unaffiliated teams on two corpora with two disjoint model sets. (1) src-0006's Table 2 restricted to its nine F1 rows -- one corpus, one 15-model set, one metric -- gives a Contextualization stage mean of 0.636 (IOC Normalization 0.656, Affected Systems 0.650, Attack Infrastructure 0.631, Malware Family Mapping 0.607) against an Attribution stage mean of 0.602 (TTP Extraction 0.673, Infrastructure Reuse 0.612, Relation Graph Building 0.610, False Flag Detection 0.511). The 0.034 gap is in the predicted direction but is roughly one eighth of the 0.272 mean between-model spread on a single task, and the best task in the subset is an Attribution-stage task. (2) src-0007's Table 4, the source that appears to support the ordering, reverses its own middle-to-third rung between two models: GPT-4o's attribution rubric of 1.140/5 normalises to 0.228 or 0.035 against a derived TTP F1 of 0.2502 (at or below), while o3-mini's 2.968/5 normalises to 0.594 or 0.492 against 0.2337 (above), under both defensible normalisations. THREE MATERIAL CAVEATS. (a) src-0006 reports no confidence intervals, no seeds and no repeat runs, so 0.034 carries no uncertainty estimate; this candidate asserts that the ordering is NOT SUPPORTED, not that the reverse ordering holds. (b) Four of the nine rows are strictly monotone decreasing across all eight general-purpose columns in printed order, a pattern of unknown cause verified as-printed by three pulls across two URL forms; dropping all four leaves 0.641 against 0.592, gap 0.049, same direction, same best task. (c) The fourth rung of the proposed ordering, open-ended GENERATION, is not represented in the commensurable subset at all, so this candidate refutes the extraction-versus-classification-versus-attribution part of the ordering and is SILENT on generation, which remains supported in the parent issue by src-0001's extraction-versus-generation confidence-interval-width split of 0.02 against 0.06.

PROPOSED, entered cycle 18 as the replacement explanatory variable this issue's inherited first open_question asked for. THE CLAIM: model identity explains as much of the variance in CTI sub-task reliability as sub-task identity does, corpus identity may explain more than either, and the extraction-versus-reasoning category is a weak third. On src-0006's nine-row commensurable F1 subset the mean between-model range within a task is 0.272 and the mean between-task range within a model is 0.263 -- equal to within 0.009 -- while the extraction-versus-reasoning stage gap on those same rows is 0.034. Separately, the same nominal sub-task, ATT&CK TTP mapping, scores F1 0.478-0.751 in src-0006 against a derived F1 of 0.157-0.250 in src-0007: a shift of roughly 0.4 on one task, larger than any between-task gap either paper reports. THREE OBJECTIONS TO ITSELF, which is why this is proposed and not supported. (i) The between-model and between-task figures are RANGES, not variance components; a range is sensitive to a single outlying model, and src-0006's LLY is an outlier on two of the nine rows (False Flag Detection 0.286, Patch Recommendation 0.442). (ii) The cross-source TTP comparison is uncontrolled -- task definition, model set, publication year and metric decomposition all differ at once -- so corpus identity is only one of at least four candidate explanations for that 0.4 shift. (iii) Both figures come from ONE study's table, and no cycle has checked whether the same equality holds in any other multi-model multi-task security evaluation; src-0014's roughly fourfold spread in prompt-sensitivity between models on identical data introduces a fourth variable, prompt strategy, that this candidate does not account for at all.

issues.title: Have AI-generated CTI failures already reached production/publication at real institutions, and how do institutions respond when caught?
open_questions:
REWRITTEN cycle 12, and deliberately reframed so it stops being answerable by anecdote. The base rate of hallucinated citations across CTI PUBLISHERS is still unmeasured and no cycle should claim otherwise: we now have two named incidents (ENISA src-0004, EY Canada src-0012), and two anecdotes are not a rate. What was found instead is the nearest systematic audit in an ADJACENT population -- src-0011 (GhostCite) manually verified 2.2M citations across 56,381 papers and reports 1.01% of papers at Security venues containing at least one invalid citation. It cannot be transferred to CTI: it audits peer-reviewed conference papers, defines a ghost citation as one absent from academic databases (inapplicable to CTI footnotes, which are news/vendor URLs), and reports per-PAPER rates that are not comparable with src-0004's per-FOOTNOTE 26/492. WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY CLOSE THIS: (a) a link-resolution/footnote-verification sweep over N published threat reports from M agencies and vendors, which is mechanically cheap since both known incidents were found precisely this way (dead links); (b) a disclosure-policy survey of CTI publishers; or (c) an existing audit of vendor/agency reports if one can be found. Cycle 12 searched for (c) and found only academic-corpus and consulting-report audits, never a CTI-publisher audit. AMENDED CYCLE 59, DISCHARGING ctr-0022 STEP (iv), AND THE AMENDMENT IS A NARROWING, NOT AN ANSWER. That closing sentence about (c) is now SUPERSEDED IN ONE SPECIFIC AND LIMITED WAY: such a sweep EXISTS AND IS RUNNING. GPTZero states verbatim 'Over the past few months we have set up an automated pipeline to search for vibe citations by finding and scanning public reports from major consulting firms.' That is exactly the link-resolution/footnote-verification sweep option (a) asks for, applied to consulting firms rather than to CTI publishers proper. BUT IT IS STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE OF SUPPLYING THE BASE RATE THIS QUESTION ASKS FOR, AND THE REASON IS ESTABLISHED AT SOURCE RATHER THAN ASSUMED: asked DIRECTLY for any total number of reports scanned, or any rate or percentage of reports found to contain hallucinated citations across the sweep, the page returned ABSENT. THE DENOMINATOR IS WITHHELD. GPTZero publishes NUMERATORS ONLY, one instalment at a time -- verbatim, 'Instead of releasing our results all at once, we are going to focus on one report at a time.' A serially-released stream of named incidents with no reported N is a source of ANECDOTES, however many of them there are, and stacking more of them will never produce a rate. CONSEQUENCE FOR FUTURE CYCLES, STATED SO THIS IS NOT REDISCOVERED: fetching GPTZero's further named investigations (a government publication and two different Deloitte reports, unfetched since cycle 13) would add INCIDENTS to this issue and is legitimate T1 work, but it CANNOT close this open question and no cycle should score it as if it could. What would still close (a) is a sweep by a party that publishes its N -- including, in principle, this loop running one itself over a named list of published threat reports, which remains mechanically cheap and undone. Cycle 13 recorded the GPTZero pipeline as 'a T1 collection lead'; no cycle in the forty-six since had recorded that the lead cannot yield a base rate as published.

===== AMENDED CYCLE 100 (T2), ON THE PROPOSED METHOD ONLY; THE BASE-RATE FINDING AND THE WITHHELD-DENOMINATOR FINDING ARE UNTOUCHED AND NO RATE IS COMPUTED HERE. This entry proposes a footnote-resolution sweep as the route to a CTI base rate. CYCLE 99 DOCUMENTED TWO FAILURE MODES THAT SUCH A SWEEP CANNOT DETECT, so the method as proposed would systematically UNDERCOUNT and any rate it produced would be a FLOOR rather than an estimate. (1) FABRICATED CLAIMS ABOUT NAMED THIRD PARTIES (src-0036): UBS, the UK's National Health Service, Swiss Federal Railways and Transport for London all told the Financial Times that the KPMG report's claims about their AI usage were 'either untrue or misleading'. A plausible false assertion about a named organisation resolves to no URL at all and is not link-checkable in principle; it was caught only because the organisations themselves rebutted it. (2) REFERENCES THAT RESOLVE BUT ANCHOR TO NO CLAIM (src-0037): verbatim, 'Another seven lack numbers and associated footnotes, meaning they aren't linked to specific claims.' A live URL attached to nothing passes a resolution check cleanly. ANY CYCLE COSTING THIS METHOD MUST NOW COST A SECOND, NON-MECHANICAL PASS ALONGSIDE IT, AND MUST NOT REPORT A SWEEP RESULT AS A BASE RATE WITHOUT SAYING WHICH FAILURE MODES IT WAS BLIND TO. SEPARATELY, AND RECORDED HERE SO IT IS NOT RE-DISCOVERED AS A CONFLICT, PER CYCLE 99's EXPLICIT G3 NOTE: src-0034 publishes a COMPLETE per-report denominator (45 citations, partitioned 5 accurate / 28 with fake components / 12 undetermined) but that is the CITATION COUNT WITHIN ONE REPORT, not the SWEEP-LEVEL NUMBER OF REPORTS SCANNED which this entry establishes at source that GPTZero withholds. THE TWO ARE DIFFERENT QUANTITIES. The sweep-level N remains unpublished across src-0032, src-0034 and src-0037 alike, this entry is UNTOUCHED by all three, and NO BASE RATE MAY BE COMPUTED FROM ANY OF THEM. Cycle 100 opened no contradiction on this point and no cycle should without new evidence.

PARTIALLY ANSWERED cycle 12, first half CLOSED. ENISA's AI usage was NOT disclosed to readers before publication and was admitted only when Der Spiegel asked after external researchers found the dead links (src-0004). Stronger now: ENISA's own publication pages for BOTH affected reports (src-0009, src-0010) carry revision notices dated 09 January 2026 describing the fix purely mechanically -- 'updated to edit some links' and 'updated to correct some broken links and typos' -- and as of 2026-07-29, roughly 8 months after exposure, NEITHER page carries any mention of AI or generative AI. So the non-disclosure was not merely pre-publication; it persists in the corrected record. STILL OPEN: whether ENISA changed any internal policy (a cycle-12 search found no published policy change), and whether any peer agency changed disclosure policy in response. Also still open at PDF level: the front matter / legal notice of the v1.2 PDFs was not pulled, so the 'no AI disclosure anywhere' claim is currently established only for the landing pages. ===== AMENDED CYCLE 72, AND THIS CLAUSE IS NOW LARGELY DISCHARGED. THE ORIGINAL WORDING IS PRESERVED ABOVE SO THE AMENDMENT IS AUDITABLE. CYCLE 72 PULLED BOTH v1.2 PDFs AND ALSO THE PRE-CORRECTION v1.1 OF THE PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION REPORT, entering them as src-0025, src-0026 and src-0027; see this issue's cycle-72 candidate_resolutions. THE LEGAL NOTICE AND ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS OF BOTH REPORTS WERE RECOVERED WHOLE, and neither PDF mentions AI, artificial intelligence, generative AI, LLM or large language model in connection with how the report was produced, written or edited. SCOPE OF THAT ABSENT, STATED EXACTLY BECAUSE IT DIFFERS BETWEEN THE TWO REPORTS AND MUST NOT BE FLATTENED: for the Public Administration report (src-0026) the render self-reported NOT TRUNCATED, so the absence is WHOLE-DOCUMENT and that report's PDF-level gap is CLOSED. For the Threat Landscape 2025 report (src-0025) the render self-reported TRUNCATED mid-Section 7 of 13, so under methodological rule (xvi) the absence is valid FOR THE FRONT MATTER AND SECTIONS 1-7 ONLY. THE FRONT-MATTER QUESTION AS THIS CLAUSE POSED IT IS THEREFORE ANSWERED FOR BOTH REPORTS; THE WHOLE-DOCUMENT QUESTION REMAINS OPEN FOR src-0025 ALONE, and closing it requires reading sections 8-13. A SPECIFIC AND NEWLY-NAMED TARGET INSIDE THAT RESIDUE: src-0025 CONTAINS A SECTION TITLED 'LOG HISTORY', LISTED AS SECTION 13, WHICH NO CYCLE HAS READ. That is where a version changelog would live and it is now the cheapest remaining route on this question. WHAT IS STILL WHOLLY OPEN AND IS UNTOUCHED BY ANY OF THE ABOVE: whether ENISA changed any internal policy, and whether any peer agency changed disclosure policy in response. A cycle-12 search found no published policy change and no cycle since has retried.

PARTIALLY ANSWERED cycle 12, and the answer for the NUMBER is no. ENISA's own primary artefacts (src-0009, src-0010) independently corroborate the STRUCTURE of the incident -- two reports, published October 1 and November 6 2025, both revised on 09 January 2026, both revisions concerning links -- exactly as src-0004 reports secondhand. But neither ENISA page gives any footnote count and neither mentions AI, so the 26-of-492 figure remains sourced to Der Spiegel via Heise and is corroborated only by outlets (cybernews, Tagesspiegel, derStandard) that themselves cite Der Spiegel, i.e. NOT independently.
